h1: Mayflower Grande Hotel Chiang Mai — a 3-star hotel in the heart of Nimman where One Nimman is just out the door
intro: Picture this: you step out of the lobby, turn a few paces, and you're already among the coffee shops, cafes, restaurants, and One Nimman lined up along the street many people call the heart of modern Chiang Mai — Mayflower Grande Hotel Chiang Mai is a 3-star hotel that sells its central Nimmanhaemin location to the full, at a price far more reachable than the luxury hotels in the same area · open since 2011 and freshly renovated in 2024 · some upper-floor rooms look out to Doi Suthep, and there's the Chili Bistro restaurant, a massage spa, and free parking · from about ฿900/night, with a real review score of 8.6 from over 1,100 reviews

body.html: Overview and who it suits — Mayflower Grande Hotel Chiang Mai is a 3-star hotel sitting right in the middle of Nimmanhaemin Road, the area many people consider the liveliest zone of modern Chiang Mai, packed with cafes, international restaurants, bars, galleries, and shopping centers · the hotel has been open since 2011, a roughly 10-storey building with about 110 rooms, and was renovated in 2024, which makes many parts feel fresher than before · what sets it apart from other hotels in the same area is the mix of a central Nimman location where you can walk to everything, with prices that start in the hundreds-to-low-thousands range, which is genuinely hard to find in this zone · pulling together the real reviews from Trip.com, Agoda, Booking, and Tripadvisor, this place suits travelers who want to base themselves in Nimman — couples, solo travelers, cafe-hoppers, shoppers, and digital workers who want a good location without blowing the budget · on the flip side, if you're after a luxury riverside resort on the Ping River, a big pool, or a quiet Lanna boutique vibe, this may not be the answer, because the main selling points are location and value, not luxury or 5-star-style amenities

Location and getting around — Mayflower Grande sits at 9 Nimmanhaemin Road, Suthep, Mueang Chiang Mai, one of the most sought-after locations for today's travelers · the upside nearly every review agrees on is that it's a few minutes' walk to One Nimman, the community mall at the center of the area, with restaurants, cafes, a market, souvenirs, and an event plaza · you can also walk comfortably to MAYA Lifestyle Shopping Center, Think Park, and the Museum of World Insects in about 5–10 minutes · the area around the hotel is full of well-known coffee shops, massage parlors, convenience stores, and side streets hiding plenty of local eateries, so you can wake up and find something to eat or a cafe to work in without planning ahead · to reach the old city inside the walls, Tha Phae Gate, and the famous temples, it's about a 10–15 min ride by songthaew (red truck) or Grab · the Night Bazaar and Chang Khlan Road are about 15 minutes away · one thing many people love is that it's only about 7 kilometers from Chiang Mai Airport (CNX), a 10–15 min drive, ideal for short trips where you want to land and check in quickly · the location note worth knowing is that Nimman is a busy, lively area all night, especially on weekends, so if you get a low floor or a street-facing room you may hear some noise from the shops and traffic, which is a point we'll cover more in the notes section below

Room types and decor — the hotel has around 110 rooms spread across a 10-storey building, divided into several tiers · the Superior Room is the entry level, around 25 sqm, on floors 3–6, available with either a King bed or Twin beds, suited to one or two people who mainly use the room as a base for exploring · above that are the Deluxe Room at around 32–40 sqm and the Executive Room at around 44–48 sqm, on floors 7–9, giving you more space and better views · after the 2024 renovation, the rooms were redone in a bright, easy-on-the-eyes palette, using wood floors and soft pastel green tones, with a work area in the room · what guests often praise is the upper-floor rooms looking out to Doi Suthep, the warm-water rain shower bathrooms, and the bathtub in some higher-tier rooms · the rooms have air conditioning, a TV, a small fridge, and free drinking water · a straight-up note from the reviews: because the building has been open since 2011, some rooms that haven't been fully renovated can look older than the newly renovated ones, and some reviews mention maintenance in certain spots, so if you care about freshness and views, specify that you want an upper-floor room on the Doi Suthep side and a renovated room when booking · overall, the starting room size of 25 sqm is just right for a 3-star hotel, and the beds and bedding earn praise for being comfortable for the price · for those coming to work or staying longer, there's a desk and Wi-Fi, making it an easy base for working in Chiang Mai
"The selling point is purely the location — step out of the hotel and you hit cafes, restaurants, and One Nimman, no need to call a car all day. Clean rooms, great value for this area."

Facilities, pool, and spa — let's be straight from the start: Mayflower Grande is a 3-star hotel focused on location and value, so there is no pool, which is worth knowing before you book, especially if you want a hotel with a pool to cool off in on this trip · what it does have is a relaxing spa and massage service inside the hotel, handy for anyone who has walked Nimman all day and wants a massage before bed · there's also a meeting room for small seminar groups, an airport transfer service (ask about the fee in advance), a bicycle rental for cycling around the area, and importantly free parking, an advantage that's hard to find for a hotel in central Nimman where space is limited · the note from reviews is that parking is limited, and during full periods it can be hard to find a spot at certain times, so if you drive yourself, keep that in mind · there's free Wi-Fi in both the rooms and common areas, and the reception desk is open 24 hours · overall the facilities are appropriate for a 3-star hotel focused on location — not a full resort kit, but enough for people who plan to spend most of their time outside the hotel exploring Nimman

Food and bar — the hotel's main restaurant is Chili Bistro, serving Thai and international food, open from midday to evening (about 8:00 AM–10:00 PM), and it's where breakfast is served for in-house guests · breakfast here is a compact buffet in the style of a 3-star hotel, with both Thai dishes and basic international options, which many reviews say is enough and good value, even if the choices aren't as varied as a big hotel · the point many see as a genuine upside is the hotel's central Nimman location — so if you don't feel like eating in the hotel, a few steps out and you'll find hundreds of restaurants, cafes, and street food to choose from, from famous khao soi spots and noodle shops to specialty coffee shops and international restaurants · put simply, food is barely an issue, because the whole area is Chiang Mai's hub for eating and drinking · the honest note from reviews is that some find the in-hotel breakfast a bit ordinary, so if you're a breakfast person, we'd suggest heading out to try the many cafes and breakfast spots in the Nimman area instead

Service — the thing that earns consistent praise in reviews here is the friendliness and helpfulness of the staff · many reviews describe the same thing: the front desk smiles, gives good recommendations on restaurants, sights, and getting around the Nimman area, helps call a songthaew or Grab, and handles check-in and check-out quickly · for a hotel at this price, the service is better than expected and one of the reasons the review scores stay consistently good · the desk is open 24 hours, making it convenient to check in late or leave early for the airport · extra services like helping book a Doi Suthep or Doi Inthanon tour, or trips around the city, can be arranged at the front desk · overall, if there's one thing that lifts the experience at this budget place, the staff's service is the clear answer

Voices from real reviews (pros and cons) — on the praise side, the points repeated over and over are the central Nimman location with a walk to One Nimman, MAYA, and countless cafes, value for money compared with the location, clean and tidy rooms, friendly and helpful staff, free parking, and the upper-floor rooms looking out to Doi Suthep · on the notes side found in some reviews are no pool, a limitation for those who want a hotel with one, some rooms not yet renovated that look older than the new ones with signs of wear, noise from the lively Nimman area especially in low-floor street-facing rooms, breakfast options that aren't very varied, and limited parking during full periods · the overall picture from over 1,100 reviews still gives an average score in the good range (around 8.5–8.7), and many couples rate the location especially high, which reflects that for people who chose this hotel for its location and price, the upsides carry more weight than the notes

Price comparison and value — the starting price for a Superior room is around ฿900–฿1,400/night in normal periods, and can climb to about ฿1,600–฿2,500/night in high season (November–February) or during big festivals like Loy Krathong–Yi Peng and New Year, while Deluxe and Executive rooms go higher depending on size and view · compared with other hotels in the Nimman area, the value here lies in getting a central Nimman location where you can walk to everything, at a price that's clearly often cheaper than design boutiques or 4–5-star hotels in the same area · if you plan to spend most of your time walking around, hitting cafes, shopping, and exploring Nimman, the money is very well spent, because you barely pay for transport at all · but if you intend to spend most of your time in the hotel relaxing resort-style, and you want a pool or a luxury atmosphere, you may need to weigh other options that offer more amenities at a higher budget · the tip is to compare prices across several platforms and book with free cancellation up front, because prices shift a fair bit by date and festival period, especially when Nimman is in high demand

Things to know before booking, and the verdict — in short, Mayflower Grande Hotel Chiang Mai is a 3-star hotel that suits people who want to base themselves in Nimman at a good price, with a location within walking distance of everything, friendly service, and clean rooms for the price · things to know before booking: one — there is no pool here, so if your trip needs a pool, choose elsewhere · two — ask for an upper-floor room on the Doi Suthep side and a renovated room if you want the view, freshness, and quiet · three — in high season and festival periods, book ahead and lock in your price because Nimman is a popular area · four — if you're sensitive to noise, avoid low-floor street-facing rooms · five — if you drive yourself, the upside is free parking, but it's limited, so arrive before evening · six — if breakfast matters to you, head out to try the many cafes and restaurants in the Nimman area · for couples, solo travelers, cafe lovers, and digital workers who want a central Nimman location on a reachable budget, this is one of the most worthwhile and convenient options in the area · just understand from the start that the selling point is location and price, not luxury or resort-style amenities, and the experience will match expectations nicely

honestSummary: Mayflower Grande Hotel Chiang Mai is the best 3-star hotel for people who want a central Nimman location within walking distance of everything, plus a good price and friendly service · but you have to accept there's no pool, the vibe is a city hotel in a lively area, not a quiet resort, and some rooms still look older than the newly renovated ones
honestChecks: If this trip needs a pool to cool off in — there's no pool here at all → consider a Nimman hotel with a rooftop pool, or a resort outside the city instead

If you're sensitive to noise and want total quiet — Nimman is lively at night, and low-floor street-facing rooms may hear noise → ask for an upper-floor room on the Doi Suthep side and a renovated room when booking

If you're booking in high season (Nov–Feb) or the Loy Krathong–New Year festivals — Nimman is a popular area, prices climb fast and rooms fill quickly → book ahead and lock in a free-cancellation rate first, then compare across several platforms

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Mayflower Grande Hotel Chiang Mai

faq.q: Where is Mayflower Grande Hotel Chiang Mai · how close is it to One Nimman?
faq.a: It's located at 9 Nimmanhaemin Road, Suthep, Mueang Chiang Mai, in the heart of the Nimman area · about a 3 min walk to One Nimman · walk to MAYA, Think Park, and the Museum of World Insects in 5–8 minutes · about a 10–15 min drive from the old city and Tha Phae Gate, and only about 7 kilometers from Chiang Mai Airport, a 10–15 min drive

faq.q: What's the starting price at Mayflower Grande Hotel Chiang Mai · what rooms are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about ฿900/night for a Superior room of ~25 sqm · there are several tiers from Superior, Deluxe Twin (~32–40 sqm), to Executive (~44–48 sqm, upper floor with Doi Suthep view, some rooms with a bathtub) · prices depend on the period and package, climbing fast in high season, so compare across several platforms before booking

faq.q: Does Mayflower Grande Hotel Chiang Mai have a pool?
faq.a: No pool · this is a 3-star hotel focused on location and value, with a massage spa service, the Chili Bistro restaurant, free parking, and bicycle rental, but no pool · if your trip needs a hotel with a pool, choose another property in the Nimman area with a rooftop pool instead

faq.q: Who does Mayflower Grande Hotel Chiang Mai suit best?
faq.a: It suits couples, solo travelers, cafe-hoppers, shoppers, and digital workers who want to base themselves in Nimman at a good price, with easy walking and no need for a car · if you're after a luxury riverside resort on the Ping River, a big pool, or a quiet Lanna boutique vibe, another property may suit you better

faq.q: Are Mayflower Grande's rooms renovated · which room should I ask for?
faq.a: The hotel opened in 2011 and was renovated in 2024, making many rooms look brighter and easier on the eyes, but not every room is renovated equally · we recommend specifying at booking or check-in that you want an upper-floor room on the Doi Suthep side and a renovated room, so you get the view, freshness, and quiet from the lively Nimman area

faq.q: Does Mayflower Grande Hotel Chiang Mai have parking?
faq.a: Yes, free parking, which is an advantage that's hard to find for a hotel in central Nimman · but the number of spots is limited, and during full periods it can be hard to find one at certain times, so if you drive yourself, we recommend arriving before evening to get a spot more easily
